transcript:
Header: 2027-04-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 51m | Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE); Tom Nguyen (Monolith AI), Sara Bloom (Infra), Carlos Reyes (Product), Ava Li (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to understand model constraints and deployment needs; customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private + open-model tradeoffs.

00:00 Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm ethan, i'm the AE on the account. maya and liam here from the SE side.
00:12 Tom: thanks, ethan. tom here. we're trying to figure out model selection for our assistant product, need to map tradeoffs.
00:20 Maya: great, can you give us a bit of context — current stack, what you run, and what success looks like?
00:30 Tom: yeah sure. currently we run a mix: internal transformers, some fine-tuned open weights, prod infra on aws EKS. latency needs are pretty strict for sync UI calls, <300ms ideally for small queries, but some longer context transcript summarization can be async.
00:50 Sara: infra note — we have gpu pools in us-east and also a dedicated on-prem rack for PII workloads. so curious about private deployment options.
01:05 Carlos: product ask — multilingual support for EN/FR/ES/JP, and ability to do tool-calling (calendar APIs, internal kb search).
01:20 Maya: ok good. on model selection — are you leaning toward higher-context models 8k+ or mostly 2k-4k?
01:30 Tom: both. main chat flows are 2k-4k but we have two big use-cases: call summarization with 10-20k context and retrieval augmented generation where we need 8k+. so context length matters.
01:50 Ethan: understood. we usually map those to a combination: compact 8k models for most RAG and a long-context variant (or chunking + streaming) for 10-20k. are you evaluating open models specifically?
02:05 Tom: yes, cost is a driver — open weights preferred, but we need quality close to Anthropic/OpenAI for hallucination control. also need tool-calling like structured function calls.
02:20 Maya: on open models — there are several families: Mistral, Llama-derivatives, Mosaic/Meta forks. Redwood's catalog has curated performance profiles. we'll send a comparison matrix but quick notes: some 8k open models will be cheaper but may require quantization or different kernel paths to hit latency targets.
02:42 Sara: how different is hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost? we want predictable throughput for prod.
02:50 Liam: hosted is fastest to get started and good for variable usage; pricing is per-token and you get our managed model variants. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, with VPC peering and data isolation. Private (on-prem) is for when you need full network control and KMS integration.
03:12 Ava: security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS/HSM for private. is that supported?
03:22 Maya: yes; hosted can provide SOC2 compliance and audit logs, but for customer-managed KMS and full air-gapped options, that's Private deployment. Dedicated supports customer VPC and controlled key management integrations as well.
03:40 Tom: on tool-calling — we rely on structured function calls from the LLM. does Redwood support function/ tool calling across open models or only certain vendors?
03:50 Liam: function-calling is supported at the API layer; for open models we wrap outputs and do schema enforcement server-side. some model variants have better structured output reliability — we can demo example flows.
04:10 Carlos: any gotchas for multilingual? e.g., fine-tuning latency or tokenization issues with JP?
04:20 Maya: tokenization differences can cause cost spikes for some languages; we recommend measuring tokens per-language. some open models have stronger multilingual coverage; we'll map that in the comparison matrix.
04:40 Tom: can we run a benchmark? realistic: RAG + tool-calls, 2k baseline and 12k long-context.
04:50 Ethan: totally. typical benchmark plan: we run hosted quick benchmark for a few models to show throughput/latency in your region, then for dedicated we can spin reserved nodes and run full 12k end-to-end to show cost/latency.
05:05 Sara: timeline — we're aiming to pick vendor by end of Q2, pilot in May.
05:15 Maya: ok so next steps are pricing + model matrix, and a technical deep-dive to scope the dedicated benchmark.
05:24 Tom: question on fallbacks — if we hit capacity on dedicated, can requests route to hosted?
05:32 Liam: yes that's a common pattern — smart routing with automatic fallback to hosted model variants. cost tradeoffs apply.
05:45 Ava: about logging: we need per-request audit logs and configurable retention. how granular are logs?
05:52 Maya: we can provide token-level cost breakdowns, per-request latency and traces; retention packages are configurable (add-on).
06:05 Carlos: curious about quantization and impact on hallucinations. any recommendations?
06:12 Maya: quantization helps cost and throughput but sometimes slightly changes output distribution. we recommend running evals on your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload.
06:30 Tom: any customers doing 20k+ context with open models on Redwood?
06:36 Ethan: yes — a couple of customers use chunking + KV-cache and a long-seq optimized runtime; we can share anonymized metrics.
06:48 Sara: network egress concerns for private — will we be able to limit outbound?
06:53 Liam: private on-prem gives full control; dedicated can be configured with VPC peering and egress rules.
07:05 Tom: product question — do you support streaming function-calls (progressively emit tool args)?
07:12 Maya: yes, streaming is supported and we can stream partial structured outputs; depends on model variant but we handle framing at the API layer.
07:25 Carlos: ok great. can you also include cost modeling for different throughput shapes? like 100 qps sustained vs spiky bursts?
07:35 Ethan: we'll add cost curves — hosted vs dedicated committed vs private infra costs.
07:45 Tom: competition — we've had quick talks with OpenAI and Anthropic; curious about Redwood advantages.
07:52 Ethan: Redwood is production-first with unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, better tooling for batching/caching and cost controls, and transparent perf profiles.
08:05 Ava: security follow-up — will you share SOC2 plus any pen-test summaries?
08:12 Maya: yes; we'll share SOC2 and our security whitepaper. for pen-tests we can provide redacted summaries.
08:25 Tom: ok let's recap — we want a matrix of models (8k vs 12-20k long context), multilingual perf, tool-call reliability, and pricing + latency profiles.
08:36 Ethan: agreed. we'll also propose benchmark plan and schedule the SE deep-dive.
08:44 Sara: one ask — can we get a short checklist of which Redwood features require Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted?
08:52 Liam: yes i'll make a short one-pager.
09:00 Carlos: any blockers on our side? we'll need redwood to sign an NDA?
09:06 Ethan: we have a standard mutual NDA we can send, and we can sign the customer's template if needed.
09:12 Tom: ok thanks, that's it from me.
09:20 Ethan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the matrix and links.

(End of recording)

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (Red wood / Redwood), occasional punctuation issues typical of automated transcripts. Links referenced during call: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (shared by Maya), security whitepaper link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper, model matrix (to be attached).
